common_name: Variegated Prairie Cordgrass (Aureomarginata Cordgrass, Gold-Striped Cordgrass)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring in moist to wet, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun; like the species, 'Aureomarginata' spreads by rhizomes and forms colonies in consistently moist ground, so give it room or install a rhizome barrier where space is limited.

directions: 'Aureomarginata' is the classic variegated selection of prairie cordgrass, its long, arching, sharply-edged leaf blades edged in creamy gold along each margin around a green center, giving the clump a bright, luminous quality from a distance that plain-green Spartina pectinata lacks. Comb-like (pectinate) flower spikes rise above the foliage on 4-6 foot stems in late summer, and the variegated leaves shift to warm gold and tan tones in fall before bleaching for winter interest. Best sited at pond margins, rain gardens, bioswales, and other consistently moist to seasonally flooded spots where its vigorous rhizomes can be allowed to run, or contained in large tubs/root-barriered beds in smaller gardens; it tolerates brief standing water better than nearly any other variegated ornamental grass. Cut back old foliage in late winter before new growth emerges to keep the variegation crisp.
